## [2025-01-01] — Project Initialised

### Added
- `CLAUDE.md` — primary context document for Claude Code: architecture, governance rules,
  DQ catalogue (DQ-01 to DQ-25), dimensional model grain statements, tech stack, scope decisions
- `.claude/rules/01-architecture.md` — medallion layer contracts, DuckDB usage rules,
  orchestration rules, file I/O rules
- `.claude/rules/02-governance.md` — PII tier definitions, HMAC pseudonymisation spec,
  free-text redaction patterns, access control permissions, audit log schema,
  full governance test requirements
- `.claude/rules/03-data-quality.md` — DQ framework contract, all 25 rule definitions
  with treatments, quarantine file schema, test requirements per rule
- `.claude/rules/04-testing.md` — test file map, fixture standards, bronze/silver/gold/
  governance test requirements, integration test spec
- `.claude/rules/05-coding-standards.md` — Python style, function design, config rules,
  error handling, path handling, CHANGELOG format enforcement
- `CHANGELOG.md` — this file; append-only project memory

### Governance
- Defined four access tiers: PII-SC (Art. 9), PII-S, PII, IND, SAFE
- Confirmed 25 known data quality issues from source data analysis
- Established HMAC-SHA256 pseudonymisation as the standard (not plain SHA256)
- Defined six free-text redaction patterns covering confirmed PII leaks in tickets and comments
- Specified `silver/restricted/` (700) and `silver/internal/` (750) permission boundary

### AI Usage
- Context files generated with Claude; no code written yet — this entry records
  the project initialisation and specification phase only

## [2026-05-04] — Phase 1: config files

### Added
- `config/field_classification.yaml` — all 106 columns across 14 source tables classified
  by tier (PII-SC / PII-S / PII / IND / SAFE) and treatment (exclude / pseudonymise /
  generalise_to_year / redact / passthrough). Key decisions:
  - `gender`, `nationality`, `marital_status` → PII-SC / exclude (never stored in any layer)
  - `national_id`, `national_id_type` → PII-S / pseudonymise
  - `base_salary`, `bonus_target_pct`, `comp_grade` → PII-S / pseudonymise
  - `tickets.description`, `ticket_comments.comment_text` → PII-S / redact (confirmed leaks)
  - `absence_requests.notes` → PII-SC / redact (excluded from internal even after redaction)
  - `absence_requests.absence_type_id` → PII-SC / exclude (fact builder adds
    is_sensitive_absence flag before governance validation)
  - Pipeline metadata columns (_ingested_at, _source_file) skipped by manifest validator
- `config/dq_rules.yaml` — DQ thresholds: implausible_dob_cutoff (1900-01-02),
  min_working_age (16), max_future_hire_days (0), sentinel_employee_ids (EMP023/888/999),
  sensitive_absence_type_ids (AT02/04/05/08), invalid_phone_patterns, duplicate_keep

### Governance
- Confirmed treatment for all PII-SC fields: gender/nationality/marital_status excluded
  from all silver layers (not pseudonymised, not stored)
- absence_type_id classified PII-SC/exclude with note that the fact builder pre-processes it
  into an is_sensitive_absence boolean before governance validation runs

### AI Usage
- Config files generated by Claude Code from data_analysis.md and governance rules;
  classification decisions follow rules/02-governance.md exactly.

## [2026-05-04] — Phase 2: Bronze Loader

### Added
- `src/ingest/bronze_loader.py` — full bronze loader with contract enforcement:
  - `ContractBreachError(ValueError)` — raised on any breaking contract violation
  - `validate_contract_definition(contracts)` — startup check for `_contract_version` and
    all required column keys; raises `ValueError` listing all defects
  - `build_pandera_schema(table_contract)` — dynamic DataFrameSchema from YAML; no hardcoded
    types; maps `str/int/float/bool/date/datetime/time` to pandera equivalents using pandas
    nullable dtypes (INT64, Float64, BooleanDtype) to match cast output
  - `load_csv(source_path, table_contract)` — reads CSV as str, casts to declared dtype, appends
    `_ingested_at` (UTC) and `_source_file`; raises `ContractBreachError` on cast failure
  - `validate_manifest_coverage(df, table_contract, table_key)` — raises `ContractBreachError`
    on any undeclared column; fires before pandera
  - `inject_missing_nullable_columns(df, table_contract)` — injects `pd.NA` for absent nullable
    columns; returns list of injected columns for audit log (non-breaking path)
  - `validate_contract(df, schema, table_contract, table_key)` — lazy pandera validation;
    classifies dtype/presence errors as breaking, check failures on nullable cols as warnings
  - `write_bronze(df, dest_path)` — atomic write via `.parquet.tmp` → rename
  - `load_all_bronze(data_dir, output_dir, contracts)` — orchestrates all 14 tables; returns
    `(keyed_dfs, bronze_audit_section)` with per-table row counts, contract versions,
    validation status; raises `ContractBreachError` immediately on any breaking violation

### Governance
- `config/data_contracts.yaml` — two contract fixes discovered during bronze testing:
  - Removed `checks: ["ge:0"]` from `base_salary` and `days_requested`: these checks are
    redundant with DQ-06 and DQ-19, which quarantine offending rows downstream. Keeping the
    checks caused `ContractBreachError` before DQ rules could run (spec conflict resolved by
    removing the contract checks, which were documented as "DQ quarantines downstream").
  - `successfactors/locations` bumped to `1.1.0`: `city`, `country`, `status` marked
    `nullable: true` — LOC07 source CSV row is malformed (missing trailing comma shifts
    `status="Active"` into `address` column, leaving `city`, `country`, `status` as null).
    The `is_complete` flag in `dim_location` (Phase 5) will handle this row correctly.

### AI Usage
- Implementation by Claude Code; two contract fixes required based on actual source data.
  Both deviations documented above. Smoke tested against all 14 source CSVs: 14/14 passed.
